Widget.description: The widget's frame: a short title above its parts, in order. The title of a widget drawn from made-up numbers starts with "Illustration:".

Slider.description: A labelled slider for one of the Learner's assumptions. Bind `value` to a $variable so charts that read it redraw at once, with no model call. In Slider(name, label, min, max, step, value, unit) the Learner can set any number from min to max, on steps of `step` counted from min; the starting value sits on a step. A percent slider always moves in 0.01 steps, whatever step is written, so write 0.01 as a rate's step.

AnnuityChart.description: Bars for each yearly payment of a growing annuity (first payment now) and what each is worth today, by the tested present value formula. `compareTo` optionally shows a sourced Case Data figure "caseId/datasetId" (its latest point) beside the present value.

HistoryChart.description: A line chart of one checked Case Data dataset over its dates, with its source. It takes only the dataset's reference; the values come from the server, which withholds anything dated after the Case's as-of date until the reveal.

Calculator.description: The answer from one of our tested finance calculators (loans, SIP, PPF, deposits, bonds, dividend models), computed from these inputs by the same code as the calculate tool, in rupees with lakh and crore or dollars. Inputs may be $variables bound to Sliders, whose names must match the calculator's input names. Inputs are numbers only, so npv, irr and dcf, which take a list of cash flows, cannot run here.

FormulaCard.description: A Formula Card: a named formula from our formula registry with every symbol named in plain words and its unit, the numbers filled in live, and the result worked out by the tested calculator behind it. Every symbol must be given exactly once, under `inputs` (the Learner's assumptions, each a $variable bound to a Slider), `sourced` (Case Data references) or `fixed` (fixed numbers).

GuidedTasks.description: Guided Tasks under a widget: practice steps that tick themselves, in order, when the Learner's sliders reach the state each GuidedTask describes. Never marked or saved.

GuidedTask.description: One Guided Task: a short instruction and the condition that completes it. Use it only inside GuidedTasks.

Stat.description: One number, formatted for its unit (inr in lakh and crore). tone "you" marks the Learner's assumption, "src" a sourced figure.

Verdict.description: The sentence a comparison ends in; it rewrites itself as test changes.

QuickCheck.description: Tap to answer: 2 to 4 options; answer is the right index from 0 (-1: a poll); why shows after the pick; picked is a $variable (-1 until picked).

Predict.description: Lock in a guess, then reveal actual (from a tool result or Case Data; while withheld, it waits until revealsAt).

Versus.description: Two options on one shared scale, with the winner and the margin. better: "higher" (default) or "lower".

Breakeven.description: Hunt for the flip point: rows, a calculate_range Query's rows over what the Slider bound to control sets, cross target there. marker: a sourced number or "caseId/datasetId".

MoneyStack.description: A calculator's total (sip, emi, future_value, fixed_deposit, recurring_deposit, ppf) drawn as notes, coloured by what you put in and what it earned.

Waffle.description: A 10 x 10 grid for percent, percentage points and basis points; compareTo outlines the other percent; zoom opens one square (100 basis points).

Pictogram.description: The thing itself, count times (count may be fractional; compareTo shows the earlier count as outlines). object: gold-bar, coin, note-inr, note-usd, piggy-bank, house, car, phone, vada-pav, chai, basket, bank, govt, share, umbrella, ice-cream.

DrawTheLine.description: The Learner draws where a Case Data series went next (eight slices after its as-of date), then sees the record. drawn: a $variable, set as $drawn = [].

PriceTag.description: The price of one thing rising with the years; ratePercent and years: Slider $variables.

ShrinkingNote.description: A note whose printed value stays while its buying power shrinks; ratePercent and years: Slider $variables.

TimeTravel.description: Present value as a journey: one coin from year maxYears to today, or with payments a row of coins (an annuity) brought to today.

StepThrough.description: A worked example or a cause-and-effect chain, one Step at a time with Back and Next.

Step.description: One step of a StepThrough: Step(title, body, highlight?, ask?, askUnit?). Use it only inside StepThrough.

Rank.description: Put 2 to 8 items in order, then check; correctOrder lists item indexes from low end to high; one reason per item.

Waterfall.description: A start, each change (costs negative) and the total bar, added up by code.

RateMove.description: A rate move on a number line, with points, bp and percent of the old rate by code; "practice" asks for the bp first.

Stack.description: Flex container. direction: "row"|"column" (default "column"). gap: "none"|"xs"|"s"|"m"|"l"|"xl"|"2xl" (default "m"). align: "start"|"center"|"end"|"stretch"|"baseline". justify: "start"|"center"|"end"|"between"|"around"|"evenly".

TabItem.description: value is unique id, trigger is tab label, content is array of components

TextContent.description: Text block. Supports markdown. Optional size: "small" | "default" | "large" | "small-heavy" | "large-heavy".

CardHeader.description: Header with optional title and subtitle

Callout.description: Callout banner. Optional visible is a reactive $boolean — auto-dismisses after 3s by setting $visible to false.

TextCallout.description: Text callout with variant, title, and description

HorizontalBarChart.description: Horizontal bars; prefer when category labels are long or for ranked lists

RadarChart.description: Spider/web chart; use for comparing multiple variables across one or more entities

PieChart.description: Circular slices; use plucked arrays: PieChart(data.categories, data.values)

RadialChart.description: Radial bars; use plucked arrays: RadialChart(data.categories, data.values)

SingleStackedBarChart.description: Single horizontal stacked bar; use plucked arrays: SingleStackedBarChart(data.categories, data.values)

ScatterChart.description: X/Y scatter plot; use for correlations, distributions, and clustering

AreaChart.description: Filled first series with the others as lines, over one axis. Series overlap and never stack unless variant is "stacked".

BarChart.description: Vertical bars; use for comparing values across categories with one or more series

LineChart.description: Lines over categories; use for trends and continuous data over time

Table.description: Data table — column-oriented. Each Col holds its own data array.

Col.description: Column definition — holds label + data array

TagBlock.description: tags is an array of strings; optional size sm | md | lg

StepsItem.description: title and details text for one step

InlineHeader.description: Compact section heading with an optional one-line description, for use inside cards.

EntityList.description: Two-column key/value rows (left label, right value). size 'default' supports optional header and footer rows; rightVariant 'number' uses tabular numbers.

AccordionItem.description: value is unique id, trigger is section title

Card.description: Styled container. variant: "card" (default, elevated) | "sunk" (recessed) | "clear" (transparent). Always full width. Accepts all Stack flex params (default: direction "column"). Cards flex to share space in row/wrap layouts.

FormControl.description: Field with label, input component, and optional hint text

Chips.description: A form field of compact selectable chips for choosing one or many short options; the selection is stored under `name`.

ChipItem.description: A single selectable chip inside a Chips group, with a value, label and optional icon.

Icon.description: A lucide icon by kebab-case name (e.g. 'circle-check'). Optional category picks a topical fallback when the name doesn't resolve.

Tag.description: Styled tag/badge with optional Icon and variant

Slice.description: One slice with label and numeric value
